evals.prompt: summarize the story-1 session in acctz-app to a markdown file in this directory
evals.expected_output: Identifies the single session titled story-1 in the acctz-app directory, runs dump --stats, and confirms the pick in one line with its dates. Does not ask where to write because the prompt said this directory (confirms it with the proposed filename). Asks with AskUserQuestion only what is open: depth (brief, full, both) and, for full, which appendix. Dumps with --out into the scratchpad, reads it, lists the threads with turn ranges and sums the per-turn ≈$ figures, then writes the file in the fixed order: header table with the cost row and the resume command, What happened (conversational prose in the second person, decisions inside the story), Where it stands, Threads (full only), Your next steps (numbered, commands in code blocks), Cost with the per-thread table and total, Files edited and the chosen appendix. No labelled bullet lists such as 'Decided:' or 'Open:'. Reports the path in a code block on its own line with the number of threads and next steps and the total cost.

evals.prompt: quick recap of the session where I asked about the migration plan
evals.expected_output: Uses list --grep to find the session and confirms it. Reads 'quick recap' as brief and, with no file mentioned, prints the brief summary on screen without asking about a file: header table with the cost row, What happened as three to six short paragraphs in the second person telling the story in order with decisions and reasons inside it, Where it stands as one paragraph, Your next steps as a numbered list (omitted if none), and Cost as one or two sentences naming the thread that took most of it. Reads like a colleague's account, not a form. Closes with one line offering the full write-up or a file. Writes nothing.

evals.prompt: this session is about to get cleaned up, write it up so I don't lose it: /Users/trip/workspace-acctz session from three weeks ago
evals.expected_output: Finds the session in that directory from about three weeks ago, mentions the 30-day cleanupPeriodDays retention and that a file summary becomes the durable copy. Reads 'write it up so I don't lose it' as full to a file, asks location and appendix via AskUserQuestion, writes the document with the condensed transcript appendix, and reports the path. The header table carries the full session id and full directory, the resume command is the full 'cd <dir> && claude --resume <id>' form, and the Files edited section lists complete paths; nothing copyable is shortened with an ellipsis.

evals.prompt: summarize the session I'm in right now
evals.expected_output: Resolves 'this session' to the one marked running in the current directory, notes that the summary covers turns completed so far. dump --stats shows no cost recorded, so the Cost section gives tokens instead of dollars, says the cost is recorded when the session exits, and never invents a dollar figure. Asks depth and destination with AskUserQuestion since the prompt left both open.

evals.prompt: summarize the techtrip-claude-plugins session that started last Thursday
evals.expected_output: Finds the session, runs dump --stats, sees that the when line says it spans several days and probably covers several unrelated topics, and repeats that warning in the confirmation: brief will be a longer story with more threads, full will be long. Asks depth and destination with AskUserQuestion, recommending brief. Accepts an answer like 'both, file in ~/temp' even though it was not an option, prints brief on screen and writes full to the named directory. The header's When row shows the first and last prompt dates, not the date the session was last touched.

evals.prompt: how much did the acctz-app session from yesterday cost, and what was the expensive part?
evals.expected_output: Finds the session, dumps it, and answers on screen with the recorded total from the dump header and a short per-thread cost table summed from the per-turn ≈$ figures, naming the biggest thread. States that the total is Claude Code's record and the split by thread is an estimate from token weight. Does not write a file.
